articles.title: Fortnite Updates: December 14 Patch Unlocks Super Styles
articles.summary: The first update to Fortnite Chapter 3, Season 1 offers Super Level Styles, balance changes and more in preparation for this year’s Winterfest.
articles.body:
The first update to Fortnite Chapter 3, Season 1 has landed. With it comes weapon balance changes, Battle Pass goodies (namely Super Styles) and more in preparation for Fortnite’s Winterfest .

Fortnite Update: December 23 Update: Super Level Styles

In Fortnite, the desire to stand out amongst other players is strong. That said, so is the ability to look like your favorite character. How does one strut their stuff as Spider-Man and also maintain a somewhat unique flare? Simple. Super Level Styles .

Super Level Styles are bonus Battle Pass unlocks that alter the look of specific Chapter 3, Season 1 skins. Most of them were already available to players who hit level 100 of the pass. This update adds more, allowing anyone past level 140 to unlock rarer variations. These include a Photo Negative, Scarlet Blackout, and Gilded Reality versions of characters like Shanta and Lt. John Llama. Even Spider-Man got some new threads

Fortnite Chapter 3, Season 1 Balance Changes

Several weapons have been tweaked since this season started. A hotfix went out last week to address certain issues. This update offers more fine tuning. The Ranger Assault Rifle sports increased accuracy and damage. The Stinger SMG and Hunter Bolt Action Sniper both got animation tweaks to better showcase how much ammo they have when you’re reloading. The Striker Pump Shotgun , on the other hand, had its accuracy and rate of fire buffed. The Auto Shotgun also got a small buff. You’ll now be able to draw the weapon quicker than before.

Not all of Fortnite’s Season 3 weapons were buffed. Not only was the MK-Seven Assault Rifle’s environmental damage decreased, it’ll be less accurate when fired from the hip. This shouldn’t be shocking to most players; the MK is an incredibly powerful weapon in the right hands and that’s before considering its accuracy when aiming down sights.

Going beyond Fortnite’s weapons, the Guzzle Juice item’s heal speed has been increased.

What's Different About Fortnite Chapter 3

Recent events in Fortnite have ushered in sweeping changes to its island map. Fans can not only expect to see altered versions of familiar places, but there will be new locations as well, including Spider-Man/Peter Parker’s own Daily Bugle.

Marvel’s iconic newspaper facility won’t be the only new area worth exploring, as The Sanctuary, The Seven’s secret base of operations, has been revealed as well.

Beyond new characters and map changes, Fortnite Chapter 3 adds new traversal mechanics. These include the ability to slide about in hopes of evading enemy fire or the new swinging mechanic that allows you to mimic Spidey’s movements.

Fortnite Chapter 3, Season 1 also introduces the biggest game-changing feature since Reboot Vans in Camps. These special locations will allow you and your squadmates to store items to be used in later matches. Not only that, it’ll also allow you heal up after taking damage.

Fans can expect new items and weapons scattered all over the island. If utilized well (and with a bit luck) they’ll be able to get multiple Victory Royales and potentially earn the new Victory Crown. This digital accolade will certainly encourage competitive play.

Fortnite: Chapter 3, Season 1 Battle Pass

It wouldn’t be a new season of Fortnite without a brand-new Battle Pass. This latest pass will offer a lot of the same – new skins, emotes, weapon wraps, etc. It also features the amazing Spider-Man. While those things are worth getting excited for, it’s Epic Games allowing players to continue earning Battle Pass XP outside of Battle Royale that’s really interesting.

Done by using the Accolade Device, Fortnite Creative Mode players can build XP gain into their created experiences. They won’t be able to set the amount, so it won't be easy for players to blast through all 100 levels. Instead, they can set XP award weight based on the number Accolade Devices they have and how frequent players are awarded.

Essentially, players won’t be able to manually type in how much XP they want their friends to earn. All of the math is done in the background in a way that keeps things balanced; players will be able to influence things based on the complexity of their created accolades but won’t be able to give out free XP.

This update comes with the usual bug fixes. What’s exciting is that these changes weren’t just to improve Fortnite but also to make way for this year’s Winterfest event. There’s been no word on what day it’ll launch, besides soon. One should expect new missions, seasonal items and more in the coming days though.

And that’s it for Fortnite’s latest update. Be sure to check back here for more Fortnite Chapter 3, Season 1 patch notes! Also, if you missed it or want to make sure you didn't miss a thing, read our breakdown of Fortnite Chapter 2's finale event and the introduction of The Rock as The Foundation.

Kenneth Seward Jr. is a freelance writer, editor, and illustrator who covers games, movies, and more. Follow him @kennyufg and on Twitch.

articles.title: Celebrate The Legend of Zelda on Switch 2 With IGN Guides
articles.body:
To celebrate the release of Nintendo Switch 2 – and the 19(!) different Zelda games that are now playable on the system – the IGN Guides team has made a few upgrades to ensure you'll have a helping hand when you most need it. Not everyone needs a walkthrough to get to the end, but we hope these new features and upgrades can inspire even the most seasoned Zelda player to return and discover something they may have missed or skipped on a previous playthrough.

Speaking of smooth sailing, we hope you’re as excited as we are to revisit one of GameCube’s best games, The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker in its original form. Yes, that means the slow-sailing and long Triforce Chart/Shard quest found in the OG version are back – and you may want to use our guide to make sure you don’t head in the wrong direction. Our Wind Waker guide was originally written in 2002, but we’ve worked on some big upgrades to make it nice and new for Switch 2! Here’s what you can expect:

The Legend of Zelda: Wind Waker Guide and Map

We have overhauled our guide and walkthrough with new high-resolution screenshots, added in-page tracking, checklists, new videos, and radically upgraded our interactive map. Instead of just showing you a desktop or mobile version of the in-game map, we have redone it from the ground up and you can now zoom in all the way and see every island, enemy platform, and submarine up close. Track which Pieces of Heart , charts , and items you’ve collected and start chasing all 135 Nintendo Gallery images to finally get that 100% completion. If you prefer video, you can even track every Treasure Chart via in-video checklists (or jump to the exact spot in the video from the guide). The guide and videos of course also address the Wii U HD vs GameCube/Switch 2 version differences so that it all works for both versions.

The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild Guide and Map

Nintendo’s biggest-ever series reboot arrived on Switch 2 with upgraded framerate and resolution. If you’re like us and you’re itching to go back and see how it plays after sinking hundreds of hours into Tears of the Kingdom, we’ve got you. As a thank you to our returning IGN Guides users, our tracking experience will be completely free for the next three months, giving you enough time to finally find and check off every Korok Seed . Each seed location comes with brief hints for those who want to figure out things on their own – or you can click through to the guide for detailed tips if you're stumped.

Here are the most popular pages for people trying to 100% the game:

The Legend of Zelda: Tears of the Kingdom Guide and Map

We’ve updated our Tears of the Kingdom guide and map to get ready for the Switch 2 re-release as well. While Nintendo hasn’t changed a ton over the original Switch release, there are some updates we’ve detailed in our guide. If you’re jumping back in to finally complete the main quest, you can start with our detailed walkthrough , or embark on the never-ending Korok hunt and track everything on our Interactive Map .

If you’re wondering what changed and need some pointers for the new Switch 2-specific features, check out these links:

The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past Guide and Map

Surprise! We quietly snuck out an update to our classic A Link to the Past guide a few weeks ago – if you’ve never played or finished this 2D openworld gem, you could do worse than playing it via Nintendo Switch Online on either Switch console. It might not have the hundreds of collectibles of its 3D successors, but there are plenty of things to discover on Link to the Past ’s dual map.

We may be a little LTTP (sorry) – but we figured “better late than never” and rolled out a complete interactive map that lets you track every Piece of Heart and discover every cave and secret hidden in the 1991 classic. We also added checklists and all-new screenshots throughout the guide to make it all shiny and new!

The Legend of Zelda: Links Awakening Guide and Map

Launched on Nintendo Switch in 2019, Link's Awakening has finally gotten the update we've all been asking for: a smooth framerate. Play it on Switch 2 and you'll be able to experience Link's most-charming adventure in a dreamy 60fps at 4K resolution. Our guide helps you get to 100% completion, including all Pieces of Heart . If you used our guide way back when, check out this cool upgrade we made to the videos featured in the guide:

You can check off the collectible figures you've collected via the on-screen checklist trackers while watching the video in embed mode.

You can also bring up the in-video checklist by clicking on the button in the lower-right corner.

The Legend of Zelda: Echoes of Wisdom Guide and Map

Players have made extensive use of our Echoes checklists -- and we can tell you that the Rock, the Table, and the Zol Echo are the most collected Echoes overall. But we were also shocked that so many players who played Echoes of Wisdom outright skipped Dampe's Automaton side quest ! With the upgraded resolution and framerate on Switch 2, you may want to take another look and get all six mechanical helpers. We made it easy by providing a handy table that you can sort and filter.

Beyond these select Zelda games and guides that received upgrades this month, there is of course plenty more Zelda to be found on Nintendo Switch 2. Whether it's the Hyrule Warriors spin-offs, Skyward Sword, the NES, Game Boy Color, and Advance classics, or our two 64-bit favorites, IGN Guides has you covered. And if enough people find our Link to the Past and Wind Waker maps helpful, maybe we'll give some of those guides some upgrades as well.

Peer Schneider originally launched IGN Guides in 1999 and is now heading up IGN Entertainment's guides, tools, and game assist teams across IGN, Map Genie, Maxroll, and Gamer Network.

HOUR ZERO will span four total episodes and will be available on IGN.com and IGN's YouTube Channel.

articles.title: The Switch 2’s VRR update doesn’t extend to third-party docks, it seems.
articles.summary:
After installing the recent version 23.0.0 update on my Nintendo Switch 2, I can’t access the VRR settings option while it’s plugged into the Jsaux OmniCentro dock (I haven’t tried Genki’s Covert Dock 3 yet). The good news is that this dock still works post-update, but the ball is in third-party makers’ court to deliver a patch that enables VRR.

articles.title: Nintendo Announces New Switch Sale Made Possible By "Tariff-Related" Refunds
articles.summary: Nintendo announces a 30% off Customer Appreciation Sale for Switch games and accessories, funded in part by tariff refunds following recent US litigation.
articles.body:
Nintendo has announced a new 'Customer Appreciation' Sale in the U.S, offering 30% off dozens of Switch games and more, starting on September 13 and running through September 26.

Select games, downloadable content, accessories, amiibo, and apparel will be discounted, although Nintendo has not yet provided a full list of the games and other products that will be included in the sale across the Nintendo eShop, Nintendo Store, and other participating retailers.

The video game giant has also said that the promotion is "made possible in part by tariff-related refunds" . The company says it "absorbed most tariff-related costs", but the refunds have helped make promotions such as this new sale possible.

Nintendo previously faced questions over what it would do with money returned after the US tariff regime was challenged. Nintendo recently raised the prices of some Switch products globally, citing a combination of factors including tariffs, rising component costs, labour and shipping.

It subsequently argued that consumers were not entitled to refunds for purchases made at those higher prices after a court ruled the tariffs illegal. Nintendo said customers had received "exactly what they bargained and paid for" and that it was not required to retroactively adjust prices following the outcome of the tariff litigation.

Nintendo also maintained that it had absorbed the tariff costs on the Switch 2 itself rather than simply passing them directly on to consumers.

Now, however, Nintendo says tariff-related refunds have helped make its latest promotion possible. The company says it absorbed most of the tariff-related costs, while the refunds have contributed towards promotions such as the new Customer Appreciation Sale.

The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time (Switch 2)

Nintendo Switch 2 Carrying Case & Screen Protector - The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Edition

Young Link amiibo - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

Young Zelda amiibo - The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time

But it's already been a fairly big week for Nintendo fans/ With the two Nintendo Directs back to back , preorders for The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time and Metroid Ravenous going live , as well as that elusive 40th Anniversary Zelda Switch 2 announcement.

Nintendo has also just released a fresh firmware update for its Switch and Switch 2 consoles , including adding VRR support while playing Switch 2 in TV mode.

You can usually find Robert lost in open-world RPG games like Elden Ring and Cyberpunk 2077. Outside of gaming, his passions include reading comics (especially Superman, Batman, and Spider-Man), taking photos, and keeping up with the latest in film and TV.

His primary coverage focuses on tracking down the best gaming deals and diving into the fast-paced world of Trading Card Games (TCGs). He regularly covers everything from the latest releases in Pokémon TCG and the most expensive cards to comprehensive Magic: The Gathering buying guides . As a massive Doctor Who fan, he also keeps a close eye on physical media deals like Doctor Who Blu-ray preorders , and occasionally steps away from commerce to contribute reviews for the site, such as his review of Doctor Who's latest season .

articles.title: 'You Get Your Tariff Money back... if You Give Them More Money' — Fans React to Nintendo's 'Customer Appreciation' Sale
articles.summary: Fans are reacting to the announcement of a unique "Customer Appreciation" sale that Nintendo claims has been "made possible in part by tariff-related refunds."
articles.body:
Fans are reacting to the announcement of a unique "Customer Appreciation" sale that Nintendo claims has been "made possible in part by tariff-related refunds."

Nintendo will temporarily reduce the price of "dozens of Nintendo Switch digital games and bundles, plus savings on select physical games, downloadable content, accessories, amiibo and apparel." Whether Nintendo Switch 2 games will also be included is unknown.

While cheaper prices are nothing to be sniffed at, the framing of this promotion — which runs for just two weeks, from September 13 through September 26 — as being funded by tariff refunds has certainly raised eyebrows.

Nintendo and numerous other companies are now recouping the money they previously handed over to the U.S. government as part of tariffs that have since been deemed illegal. Nintendo (and again, numerous other companies) raised prices to combat these tariffs , and fans have been calling for Nintendo to pass some of its tariff refund back to gamers. Indeed, a proposed class action lawsuit is brewing, calling for Nintendo to share its refund with Switch purchasers — but the company itself has argued that it has no reason to do so .

Today's sale announcement is being taken by some fans as a way to placate those fans who remain upset about all this, while also continuing to signal that it won't be doling out partial refunds to any recent Switch and Switch 2 customers.

While the lack of partial refunds isn't particularly surprising, what is rather remarkable here is the acknowledgement that Nintendo did very well out of the whole situation — to the extent that it is now lowering prices (by a small amount, on a selection of titles, for a limited time).

"Ah yes, because they couldn't have possibly had a sale if it wasn't for the tariffs," wrote one fan on video game forum ResetEra .

"It's a coupon. Makes them look good and gets people to spend money. Win-win for them," wrote another.

"Lol the gall of them," wrote a third. "'We'll do a sale to celebrate not giving your money back.'"

"Nintendo is f***ing allergic to any percentage higher than 30%," wrote yet another fan. "Still, the fact that they're offering a discount at all as some sort of 'apology' is surprising in itself."

Nintendo is yet to reveal exactly which games and other products will be part of the sale, and we may not find out until the price reductions go live on September 13. But even despite the scepticism, there are plenty of fans who have already expressed excitement for the sale, and who sound ready to splash out further.

"So you get your tariff money back... if you give them more money," concluded one fan. "You know what? I'll take it lol."

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: GTA 4 Was the Xbox 360’s ‘We Mean Business’ Moment Against the PS3
articles.summary: I’d argue that GTA 4’s simultaneous release on Xbox 360 and subsequent exclusive DLC might’ve been where the Xbox brand peaked from a cultural perspective. You had to have an Xbox 360 – if not for the killer lineup of games it already had, then for the exclusive GTA 4 expansions. It was right up there with the release of Halo 3 in 2007. In fact, Fall of 2007 – which saw the release of Halo 3, Mass Effect, BioShock, Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, Rock Band, and Assassin’s Creed – through GTA 4’s release in April of 2008 might be the best six-or-so-month run any console has ever had.
articles.body:
This is an IGN opinion piece from Ryan McCaffrey, who worked at Official Xbox Magazine from 2002-2012 during the original Xbox and Xbox 360 era before joining IGN, where he remains “the Xbox guy.” In the run-up to Xbox’s 25th anniversary, he’ll be sharing his memories from the platform’s first quarter-century.

As the hugely anticipated release of GTA 6 is now just over two months away, it’s worth remembering how it wasn’t so long ago that the Grand Theft Auto games were PlayStation exclusives. GTA 3 and Vice City didn’t see the light of day on the original Xbox until November of 2003 when the pair shipped as the GTA Double Pack, meaning that GTA 3 was exclusive to PS2 for two years and Vice City for one. San Andreas, meanwhile, hit Xbox in June of 2005, a comparatively short eight months after its initial PS2 release.

The point is, when then-Head of Xbox Peter Moore – easily the best showman that’s ever run the Xbox business – rolled up his sleeve to reveal a “tattoo” of the Grand Theft Auto IV logo on his bicep at E3 2006 and announce that not only would Rockstar’s next-gen GTA ship day-and-date on the Xbox 360, but that Xbox would get not one but two timed-exclusive expansion packs (which later turned out to be the excellent The Lost and Damned and the absolutely sublime The Ballad of Gay Tony), it was the biggest of big deals. Microsoft cut Rockstar a $50 million check for the privilege, but it was worth it. At least to Xbox 360 gamers, many of whom had invested in Microsoft’s first-to-market HD Era next-gen console after its incredibly strong out-of-the-gate showing with games like Call of Duty 2 , The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion , Ghost Recon Advanced Warfighter, and Fight Night Round 3 all being verified next-gen powerhouses before the E3 2006 Xbox press conference – and before the PS3 even shipped.

Microsoft had gotten off to a huge start (as Moore used to say, “The first one to 10 million wins”), and with this GTA 4 deal, the company had shown that it was standing behind the millions of gamers who had “jumped in” with the Xbox 360 in its early days. Xbox 360 gamers wouldn’t be second-class citizens when it came to the industry’s biggest franchise.

And when GTA 4 finally got released in April of 2008 (after a delay from Fall 2007), it was, of course, a from-the-ground-up masterpiece that shared nothing in common, technologically speaking, with the GTA 3 trilogy. It took us back to Liberty City, albeit a completely reimagined one that looked incredible and was packed with small details and stuff to do. It is, in my humble opinion, the funniest of all of the satirically brilliant GTA games, as it featured the hilarious in-game internet (accessible at internet cafes…remember those?), memorable characters like Brucie, and laugh-out-loud in-universe TV shows like “The Men’s Room.”

Speaking very personally, it also came out very shortly after I got divorced, and I have really meaningful memories of my best friend Robert flying up from Arizona right after it came out to keep me company and enjoy the game with me. There was no GTA Online back then, of course, so we’d just pass the controller back and forth, each reveling in (and laughing along with) the crazy antics of the person with the gamepad in their hand. We must’ve put a few dozen hours into GTA 4 in the few days he stayed with me, and I’ll always associate GTA 4 with a much-needed bit of fun and levity and friendship in a moment when I needed it most.

Later, as I mentioned, The Lost and the Damned dropped (and stayed exclusive to Xbox for over a year), and its focus on the biker gang of the same name was a super cool pivot on the typical GTA formula. And later still, The Ballad of Gay Tony (a six-month Xbox 360 exclusive) featured impeccable storytelling and character work by Rockstar; heck, I’d personally rank it among the best DLCs or expansions for any game, ever. And then at the tail end of the Xbox 360 generation we got GTA 5…though sadly no single-player DLC at all, as originally promised, let alone exclusive DLC.

Anyway, I’d argue that GTA 4’s simultaneous release on Xbox 360 and subsequent exclusive DLC might’ve been where the Xbox brand peaked from a cultural perspective. You had to have an Xbox 360 – if not for the killer lineup of games it already had, then for the exclusive GTA 4 expansions. It was right up there with the release of Halo 3 in 2007. In fact, Fall of 2007 – which saw the release of Halo 3, Mass Effect, BioShock, Call of Duty 4: Modern Warfare, Rock Band, and Assassin’s Creed – through GTA 4’s release in April of 2008 might be the best six-or-so-month run any console has ever had.

Ryan McCaffrey is IGN's executive editor of previews and host of IGN's weekly Xbox show, Podcast Unlocked , and a co-host of Next-Gen Console Watch . He's a North Jersey guy, so it's "Taylor ham," not "pork roll." Debate it with him on Twitter at @DMC_Ryan .

articles.title: Professor Layton and the Curious Village Remake Announced, Coming to Multiple Platforms in 2027
articles.summary: A Professor Layton and the Curious Village remake has been announced by series developer Level-5.
articles.body:
A Professor Layton and the Curious Village remake has been announced by series developer Level-5.

Revealed today during the Level-5 Vision 2026 Showcase, this fresh version of the classic puzzle game will arrive at some point in 2027 for Nintendo Switch, Switch 2, PC via Steam and PlayStation 5.

A press release notes that the remake's characters have been reimagined in 3D, while the world of St. Mystere has been made more immersive with greater depth and richer detail. Professor Layton and the Curious Village's animated cutscenes have also been given a lick of paint, with higher resolution and widescreen formatting.

🆕 Annonce – Professeur Layton et l’étrange village Remake sortira sur Nintendo Switch 2 et Nintendo Switch en 2027, découvrez la première bande-annonce du jeu. pic.twitter.com/cuhbyIpMbH — NintendHOME – News & Opinions Nintendo (@NintendHOME) September 10, 2026

🆕 Annonce – Professeur Layton et l’étrange village Remake sortira sur Nintendo Switch 2 et Nintendo Switch en 2027, découvrez la première bande-annonce du jeu. pic.twitter.com/cuhbyIpMbH

Next year will mark the 20th anniversary of Professor Layton and the Curious Village's original release back on Nintendo DS, kickstarting a series that now extends to two trilogies of games featuring Professor Hershel Layton and his apprentice Luke Triton, plus further spinoffs and a memorable crossover with Phoenix Wright: Ace Attorney.

An all-new Professor Layton game is also on the way, of course: Professor Layton and the New World of Steam , which is set to launch for Switch, Switch, PC and PS5 on December 10.

Professor Layton and the New World of Steam Level 5 Vision Trailer Stills

Will further remakes follow? That may depend on how well Professor Layton and the Curious Village performs. But for anyone wanting to see how the series started on modern hardware, this remake may end up well worth a look.

Tom Phillips is IGN's News Editor. You can reach Tom at tom_phillips@ign.com or find him on Bluesky @tomphillipseg.bsky.social

articles.title: This Avengers: Doomsday Figure Reveals a Closer Look at Doctor Doom's Alternate Costume
articles.summary: Robert Downey, Jr.'s Doctor Doom will wear at least two costumes in Avengers: Doomsday, and a new action figure gives us a much better look at his alternate suit of armor.
articles.body:
Robert Downey, Jr.'s Iron Man rarely stuck to just one suit of armor in his many MCU appearances, and it appears that the same will hold true for Downey's new character, Doctor Doom. Doom will wear at least two distinct suits of armor in Avengers: Doomsday , and now we've gotten a much better look at his secondary costume thanks to a new Hot Toys figure.

Having already revealed their standard Doctor Doom figure , Hot Toys and Sideshow Collectibles have now debuted the companion Victor von Doom figure. Get a closer look in the slideshow gallery below:

Hot Toys Avengers: Doomsday Victor von Doom Figure

While this armor follows the same traditional Doom design aesthetic (green cloak and metal mask), it's quite a bit different from the other Doom suit seen in the film. It seems to be less an actual suit of armor and more a piece of regal formal wear. The green suit is more muted in color and completely covers up the armored components here. The mask is also completely different - smoother and less aggressive than the one on the Doctor Doom armor.

This suit appears to be the same one Downey's character was wearing during his initial appearance in the post-credits scene of The Fantastic Four: First Steps . Our best guess is that Doom will wear this suit in the early portions of Avengers: Doomsday, before his true power and motivations are made clear to Earth's Mightiest Heroes.

Sideshow hasn't yet put the Victor von Doom figure up for preorder. But if the Doctor Doom figure is any indication, we'd expect it to cost around $285 and release in late 2027.

Avengers: Doomsday hits theaters on December 18. Fans can get an early tease for the movie in the form of Avengers: Endgame Encore, which is set to be the longest MCU movie to date . Marvel also teased Doomsday by recreating the trailer in LEGO form .

articles.title: GTA 6's Limited Edition PS5 Controller Pre-Orders Overload PlayStation's Store, and Scalpers Are Already Reselling Them on eBay
articles.summary: Pre-orders went live for Grand Theft Auto 6's new PS5 controllers this morning and the experience was extremely chaotic.
articles.body:
Pre-orders went live for Grand Theft Auto 6's new PS5 controllers this morning, and the experience was extremely chaotic.

As you might expect, there's a ravenous demand for anything related to GTA 6. When Sony announced that they'd be opening up pre-orders for a pair of limited edition GTA 6-themed PS5 controllers last week, it was a safe bet that there'd be scalpers, store errors, and other disruptions in abundance — and that's exactly what happened when pre-orders opened this morning .

I got into a queue on PlayStation's online store half an hour before pre-orders began, and once the flood gates were opened, I was kicked to the back the line with an hour+ wait time. Thankfully, that time was quickly cut in half, likely from people unwilling to wait that long and leaving the queue, but even then, I still had issues. PlayStation's website kept giving me an error when I tried to sign into my account, forcing me to open the store in a new browser on another device. Eventually, I got through, but it was friction I could've done without.

So far, the controllers appear to be selling out at various retailers, though there is still some availability at the time of writing. GameStop and Best Buy are sold out of the white controller, while Target and Amazon appear to have them stock. Meanwhile, the black controller is exclusive to PlayStation Direct and appears to still be availabile.

PlayStation has implemented a system where users can only purchase one controller per account, which will likely limit some scalping, but not eradicate the issue. The controllers are currently being resold for nearly double the price on eBay, though it remains to be seen if people will actually buy them. It's unclear how long these controllers will remain in stock and if there will be a restock if they sell out.

With the release of pre-orders for the controller, we are just a little over two months away from the release of Grand Theft Auto 6. Marketing is in full swing now, though it's unclear what will come next. Will there be another trailer for the game following the expansive, in-depth gameplay reveal ? Will Rockstar talk about GTA Online before release ? There are still a lot of questions, but at least we are in the endgame.

Grand Theft Auto 6 will release on November 19 for PS5 and Xbox Series X|S.
